name: James
bio: James, son of Zebedee, was mending fishing nets with his father and brother John when Jesus called the two brothers to follow him; they immediately left the boat and their father to do so (Matthew 4:21-22). His place among Jesus's closest disciples is told in detail in the chapters ahead. He, along with Peter and his brother John, was taken by Jesus up a mountain to witness his transfiguration with Moses and Elijah (Matthew 17:1-8). On the way to Jerusalem, his mother asked Jesus that he and his brother John sit at Jesus's right and left in his kingdom; Jesus told them they would share his suffering, though such honors were the Father's to grant (Matthew 20:20-23). He, along with Peter and his brother John, was taken by Jesus deeper into Gethsemane to pray, though he fell asleep each time Jesus checked on them (Matthew 26:36-45). When Jesus named the twelve apostles, he surnamed James and his brother John "Boanerges," meaning "sons of thunder" (Mark 3:17). When a Samaritan village refused to receive Jesus as he set out for Jerusalem, James and his brother John asked if he wanted them to call down fire on it as Elijah had done; Jesus rebuked them for the suggestion (Luke 9:51-56).
